academic_claims.claim: French BIG portfolios split at the NYSE median market cap (so BIG is not the S&P 500); momentum sort on prior 2-12 return with 30/70 NYSE breakpoints
academic_claims.note: Page: 'The monthly size breakpoint is the median NYSE market equity. The monthly prior (2-12) return breakpoints are the 30th and 70th NYSE percentiles.' The report's '~1,000+ names' count is not stated on the page (not verified).

academic_claims.claim: French 25 size x net-issuance portfolios: NI = change in log split-adjusted shares, NYSE breakpoints, formed each June
academic_claims.note: Page: 'NI for June of year t is the change in the natural log of split-adjusted shares outstanding from the fiscal yearend in t-2 to the fiscal yearend in t-1. The NI breakpoints are NYSE quintiles.'

Jegadeesh and Titman, Journal of Finance 48(1), 65-91, March 1993. The brief never names the paper; the report itself marks any causal 'publication caused decay' claim unverified (docs/research/2026-10-20-momentum-french-screen-nogo.md:91-92).

academic_claims.claim: Robust profitability and investment were formally introduced circa 2013-2015 (Novy-Marx 2013; Fama and French 2015), so 1963-2012 is retrospective
academic_claims.note: PARTLY ACCURATE. Both papers exist as cited (Novy-Marx, JFE 108(1) 2013, gross profitability; Fama-French, JFE 116 2015, 'A five-factor model ... performs better than the three-factor model'). But Fama-French 2015's own introduction cites earlier evidence: 'Aharoni, Grundy, and Zeng (2013) document ... investment ... (See also Haugen and Baker, 1996, ... Titman et al., 2004, Fama and French, 2006...)'. Novy-Marx measures gross, not 'robust' (operating) profitability. 'Formally introduced circa 2013-2015' is a simplification; the effect on the screen is small because A2 starts in 1994 either way.

academic_claims.claim: Pontiff and Woodgate (2008) documented the share-issuance relation
academic_claims.note: Abstract (via search index; publisher page returned 403 to direct fetch): 'Post-1970, share issuance exhibits a strong cross-sectional ability to predict stock returns ... We estimate the issuance relation pre-1970 and find no statistically significant predictive ability.' Note the pre-1970 null, which the repo brief does not mention; the screen's 1963-07 start includes 1963-1969.

academic_claims.claim: McLean and Pontiff (2016) find post-publication decay across anomalies
academic_claims.note: Abstract: '97 variables ... Portfolio returns are 26% lower out-of-sample and 58% lower post-publication.' The brief says these mostly examine long-short spreads, not long-only BIG legs; that caveat is correct.

academic_claims.claim: Hou, Xue and Zhang (2020) find weak replication across anomalies
academic_claims.note: Abstract: '65% of the 452 anomalies ... cannot clear the single test hurdle of the absolute t-value of 1.96. Imposing the higher multiple test hurdle of 2.78 ... raises the failure rate to 82%.' (OUP page 403 on direct fetch; abstract via RePEc/search index.)

academic_claims.claim: Hartley & Schwarz (2019): long Treasuries over the last few days of the month, Sharpe around 1, sample 1990-2018, ~20 bp/month at 10y
academic_claims.note: Paper: 'A long Treasury position for just the last few days of each month gives a high annualized Sharpe ratio of around 1'; 'We consider data from January 1990 to the end of 2018'; 'excess returns of around 20 basis points per month at the 10-year maturity'; also 'around 25 basis points per month' on the 10-year note in a later section. The '0.25% over the last 3 days' wording in the extraction was not separately located.

academic_claims.claim: Bianchi & Goldberg (arXiv 2604.27287): over 2022-23 S&P +0.076%, SSO -11.09%, UPRO -28.24%; two-thirds variance drag; covariance term -2.24 pts/yr SSO, -5.64 UPRO
academic_claims.note: Paper: index 'was up slightly, earning a cumulative return of 0.076%'; 'SSO and UPRO were down, earning -11.09% and -28.24%'; abstract 'Roughly two-thirds ... compounding and volatility'; Table 3 Cov row -2.242 (SSO), -5.643 (UPRO). Sample starts 2022-01-03.

academic_claims.claim: Gao, Han, Li and Zhou (2018): first-half-hour timing strategy 6.67% annualized mean, Sharpe 1.08 (Table 6)
academic_claims.note: Journal of Financial Economics 129 (2018) 394-414; Table 6 row eta(r1): 6.67*** mean, Sharpe 1.08; text: 'resulting in a Sharpe ratio of 1.08'. Long/short rule (-r13 if r1 <= 0) as the repo states.
